title: Hyperlipidemia
desc: Hypertriglyceridemia in dogs — low-fat diet, chitosan fibre, omega-3, bezafibrate, plus the clinical signs that follow a rising triglyceride level.

meds.name: Low-fat diet
meds.doseText: only the low-fat diet we have recommended
meds.note: Recheck fasting triglycerides after 1 month. The goal is under 500 mg/dL.

meds.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
meds.note: 70–100 mg/kg/DAY. This is the combined EPA + DHA amount, not the total fish-oil weight.

meds.name: Bezafibrate
meds.note: Reference case from the sheet: a 40 lb dog was maintained on 100 mg once daily.

notes.When to act: Most clinical signs occur once triglycerides are above 500 mg/dL (5.65 mmol/L), but many patients show no signs even above 1,000 mg/dL (11.3 mmol/L).
notes.Confirm before treating: If the first result was not from a fasted sample, recheck a value above 500 mg/dL on a fasted sample. If it is still above 500 mg/dL, look for an underlying cause.
notes.Abdominal signs: Anorexia, vomiting, diarrhea. Acute necrotizing pancreatitis.
notes.Ocular signs: Lipid keratopathy, arcus lipoides, stromal dystrophy, lipid in the aqueous humor, uveitis, blindness, and lipemia retinalis.
notes.Skin signs: Cutaneous xanthomata, pruritus, and alopecia. Xanthomas may also occur in liver, spleen, kidney, heart, skeletal muscle and intestine.
notes.Neurological signs: Seizures, behavioural changes, neuropathies and cerebral atherosclerosis. These usually do not appear until triglycerides exceed 1,000 mg/dL.

dischargeBlocks.title: Diet
dischargeBlocks.text:
The single most important part of treatment is a low-fat diet.

- Feed only the diet we have recommended.
- No table scraps, fatty treats, chews, or food used to hide pills unless we have said it is low fat.
- Everyone in the household needs to know, or the diet will not work.

dischargeBlocks.title: Recheck bloodwork
dischargeBlocks.text:
We need to recheck {name}'s triglyceride level after about one month on the new diet.

This test must be done fasted — no food for 12 hours beforehand. Water is fine. A non-fasted sample cannot be interpreted.

dischargeBlocks.title: Call us if you notice
dischargeBlocks.text:
- Not eating, vomiting, or diarrhea
- A painful or bloated belly, or a hunched posture
- Cloudiness or colour change in the eyes, or bumping into things
- Lumps or crusty patches in the skin
- A seizure or any sudden change in behaviour

High triglycerides can cause pancreatitis, which needs to be treated quickly.

dischargeBlocks.title: Follow up
dischargeBlocks.text: Please book {name}'s fasted recheck for about one month from today. Call us sooner if any of the signs above appear.
